answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a time-delayed vault before it may transact. The stake is not a fee: it is released only after the agent completes verified work over several epochs, so creating thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of stakes at once. Like a river that cannot be dammed by scattering a walnut shell across it, cheap copies cannot redirect the flow of trust, because trust follows the slow, auditable release of staked work, not the sheer number of accounts.
